Apple is stepping up once again to donate to the relief efforts of a deadly natural disaster. Here are the details.

Apple Pledges Donation to Support Nepal as Deadly Floods Hit

Apple CEO Tim Cook said tonight that the company would be donating to support relief and recovery efforts in Nepal and Tibet, where hundreds have died from flash floods and landslides.

The disaster began on Wednesday when the lower portion of a Himalayan glacier collapsed. The debris temporarily blocked a river before bursting, sending a torrent of mud and water downstream that killed hundreds, left countless homeless, and destroyed multiple villages, roads, bridges, and other infrastructure.

Cook's pledge comes just days after Apple announced it would be donating to support earthquake relief efforts in Indonesia, and over the past several months, the company has made similar donations in response to突发事件 in Venezuela, Southern Europe, and Japan.

Beyond contributing money to natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also runs an internal donation program called Employee Giving, which has raised more than $880 million to date through a matching donation policy.
